study_identification.title: Individual differences v. the average patient: mapping the heterogeneity in ADHD using normative models

study_characteristics.study_objective: The paper aims to map the heterogeneity in brain structure of adults with persistent ADHD at an individual level using a normative modeling approach, and to investigate the degree to which case-control analyses disguise differences between individuals.

response_variable.answer: Gray matter volume; White matter volume

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper does not mention any specific methods to handle nuisance structures.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper states that 10-fold cross-validation was used for healthy individuals.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The normative range for this model in healthy individuals was estimated using 10-fold crossvalidation, then we applied the model trained on all healthy individuals to participants with ADHD.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not mention validation on an independent dataset from the same domain.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not mention validation on a dataset from a different domain.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: We tested for associations between diagnosis and those scores using a nonparametric χ 2 test in a general linear model. We corrected for multiple comparisons using the Bonferroni-Holm method (Holm, 1979). We created individualized maps of extreme deviations and calculated the voxel-wise overlap between individuals from the same groups. In a final analysis, we tested for associations between the percentage of extremely deviating voxels and age, symptom scores, and comorbidity. We corrected for the number of correlations (8) and modality using the Bonferroni-Holm method (Holm, 1979).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Case-control comparisons disguise inter-individual differences in brain biology in individuals with persistent ADHD, and the 'average ADHD patient' has limited informative value.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: At the level of the individual, deviations from the normative model were frequent in persistent ADHD. However, the overlap of more than 2% between participants with ADHD was only observed in few brain loci. On average, participants with ADHD showed significantly reduced gray matter in the cerebellum and hippocampus compared to healthy individuals. While the case-control differences were in line with the literature on ADHD, individuals with ADHD only marginally reflected these group differences.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: First, we had to use 10-fold cross-validation in healthy individuals and out of sample predictions in individuals with persistent ADHD, as our healthy sample was too small to split it into two. This potentially introduces a small bias. Second, we did not find associations of symptom scores with the percentage of deviation from the normative model. However, the measures we used to assess symptoms rely on self-report, which is generally noisier than measures from diagnostic interviews. Finally, our sample did not allow to inspect the effect of comorbidities and other potentially confounding factors on the obtained results as the comorbidities were inconsistent across individuals.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: In future studies, we envision that normative models are built on the basis of large population samples. These population-based normative models can subsequently be applied to cohorts that sample ADHD using the same inclusion criteria for healthy individuals as for those with a disorder. In this way normative modeling is complementary to classical casecontrol comparisons as it allows for the investigation of individual differences.
